key_insight: The paper introduces a filtering framework that combines coarse-graining with volume-penalization to quantify interscale energy transfer at solid boundaries, including linear transfers that standard Fourier or filtering diagnostics miss.
engineering_relevance: This gives engineers and geophysical modelers a way to measure boundary-driven energy exchange in bounded flows, improving analysis of oceanic boundary layers, wave reflections, and other multi-scale wall-bounded systems.
method: Coarse-grain the flow to separate large and small scales.
Use volume-penalization to represent the solid boundary and its influence on energy transfer.
Apply the combined diagnostic to capture linear down-scale transfer near a western boundary during Rossby wave reflection.
evidence_signal: The method is demonstrated conceptually and by quantifying down-scale energy transfer in a Rossby wave reflection off a western boundary.
watch_item: The approach is tailored to bounded flows and may require careful implementation to ensure the coarse-graining and penalization accurately represent boundary-layer physics without introducing spurious transfer signals.
paper_title: A Methodology to Quantify Interscale Energy Transfer at Solid Boundaries
